How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council. Please note that interactions between the City
Council, City staff, and the public during meetings are subject to the City’s Rules of
Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, May 20, 2025

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Chan, Council Members Ding, Herrera
  Avila, Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and

  City Council requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of May 6, 2025.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 20, 2025  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – APRIL 2025

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render and investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for April 2025.

  D. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MOSS LEVY AND
  HARTZHEIM FOR AUDITING SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $107,930
  OVER A THREE-YEAR TERM

  The City of San Gabriel is required to undergo annual independent financial
  audits in accordance with Government Auditing Standards. The current
  agreement for auditing services has concluded, necessitating the selection of a
  qualified certified public accounting firm to conduct the City’s audits. Moss Levy
  and Hartzheim (MLH) submitted the most competitive proposal and brings
  extensive municipal audit experience, strong references, and a successful
  history of working with the City. The total cost of the proposed three-year
  agreement is $107,930. The annual contract amount has been incorporated into
  the City’s annual General Fund operating budget for auditing services and does
  not require additional appropriations at this time.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a three-year agreement, with two optional one-year extensions, with Moss Levy
  and Hartzheim, LLP for professional auditing services.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 20, 2025  3
   E. REPLACEMENT OF THE FUEL TANK FOR THE EMERGENCY GENERATOR
  LOCATED AT THE PUBLIC WORKS FACILITY BY AFFORDABLE GENERATOR
  SERVICES, INCORPORATED AT A TOTAL COST OF $34,219.69

  The emergency generator at the Public Works Facility has not been properly
  maintained for a long period of time, further contributing to its declining
  performance and need for frequent repairs. To ensure the facility remains
  equipped with a dependable backup power source to the fuel station and
  power to the building, staff recommends replacing the generator base fuel
  tank. The adopted Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget included $25,000 from the
  Fleet Services Budget Account No. 124-800-37-99-730 for the purchase of a
  new generator base fuel tank. However, given the nature of the expense not
  being fleet related, the expenditure is more appropriately categorized as a
  facility-related cost rather than a Fleet Services expense and will need to be
  paid from the General Fund. These budgeted funds in Fleet Services will be
  released from appropriation. The total cost of the replacement tank, including
  sales tax, is $34,219.69.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to approve
  a purchase order with Affordable Generator Services, Incorporated for the
  replacement of the emergency generator base fuel tank located at the Public
  Works Facility, at a total cost of $34,219.69. Given the nature of the expense,
  staff recommends utilizing General Fund dollars from Budget Account No. 124-
  800-15-99-730 to cover the purchase, ensuring proper financial alignment with
  the intended purpose of the expenditure.

  F. COUNTYWIDE HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS COLLECTION PROGRAM SITING
  LIABILITY AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY

  The County of Los Angeles and the Sanitation District of Los Angeles have
  scheduled Saturday, July 19, 2025, to co-host the Annual Countywide
  Household Hazardous and Electronic Waste Collection Event at the Mission
  Playhouse Parking Lot in San Gabriel. There is no fiscal impact associated with
  executing this Agreement.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 20, 2025  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the Countywide Household Hazardous Waste Collection Program Siting
  Liability Agreement.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PROPOSED CITYWIDE FEE SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026

  The citywide fee schedule establishes user fees and charges for various
  department services. On an annual basis, the citywide fee schedule is reviewed
  and updated based on a combination of department input and the consumer
  price index in the Los Angeles Metro area. The proposed updated citywide fee
  schedule for Fiscal Year 2025-2026 is presented to the City Council for review,
  direction, and consideration of adoption. Based on the Fiscal Year 2025-2026
  forecasted revenues, a 3.3% increase to the General Fund fees is estimated to
  generate an additional $211,000 in General Fund revenue.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-19 updating
  the Master Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2025-2026.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. COMPREHENSIVE CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION STUDY REPORT

  During the last round of the labor negotiations, the City agreed to conduct a
  comprehensive classification and compensation study for Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025. In June 2024, staff selected MGT Consulting Group (MGT) to conduct the
  study. Over the last several months, MGT conducted an in-depth,
  comprehensive study of the City’s classification, compensation, and fringe
  benefit programs. The objectives of the study were to review and update the
  City’s full-time position classification and compensation systems and provide
  information pertaining to the City’s market standing for compensation and
  fringe benefits. The Classification and Compensation Report is provided for
  informational purposes only. Any salary and fringe benefit increases and/or

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 20, 2025  5
   additions made in accordance with the recommendations made in the report
  will have a substantial cost impact and must be fully assessed before the City
  commits to implementing any such increases and/or additions.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Comprehensive
  Classification and Compensation Study Report for informational purposes.

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, June 3, 2025, at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF MAY 20, 2025
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Counci l to order at
  6:32 P.M . on Tuesday, May 20, 2025, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  Eric Chan, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief
  Steven Wallace; Human Resources/Risk Management
  Director Edward Macias, Finance Director William
  Kaholokula, Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Acting Public
  Works Director John Gonzalez, Acting Community
  Development Director Samantha Tewasart, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. STROKE AWARENESS MONTH

I  Council Member Chan made the presentation and Mindy Park accepted the
  proclamation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Wu, seconded by Vice Mayor Chan, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4F as presented .

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  May 20, 2025
   Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HERRERA AVILA, WU, CHAN, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

I  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of May 6, 2025.
  2. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of May 6, 2025.
  3. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of May 8, 2025.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved April 24 and May 1, 2025, Material Demands for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - APRIL 2025

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for April 2025.

  D. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MOSS LEVY AND HARTZHEIM
  FOR AUDITING SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $107,930 OVER A THREE-VEAR
  TERM

I  The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute a three-year agreement,
  with two optional one-year extensions, with Moss Levy and Hartzheim, LLP for
  professional auditing services.

  E. REPLACEMENT OF THE FUEL TANK FOR THE EMERGENCY GENERATOR
  LOCATED AT THE PUBLIC WORKS FACILITY BY AFFORDABLE GENERATOR
  SERVICES, INCORPORATED AT A TOTAL COST OF $34,219.69

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to approve a purchase order with
  Affordable Generator Services, Incorporated for the replacement of the emergency
  generator base fuel tank located at the Public Works Facility, at a total cost of
  $34,219.69.

  F. COUNTVWIDE HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS COLLECTION PROGRAM SITING
  LIABILITY AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute the Countywide
  Household Hazardous Waste Collection Program Siting Liability Agreement.

I  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PROPOSED CITYWIDE FEE SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL VEAR 2025-2026

  Assistant Finance Director Linda Tang made the staff presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included methodology for calculating fees; staffing levels for
  Mission Playhouse events; Consumer Price Index (CPI) application to fees;
  employee discounts; the importance of the fiscal impact being highlighted; and
  allowing City commissioners to receive the same discounts as employees.
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 4  May 20, 2025
   There was no public comment; therefore, Mayor Menchaca closed the public
  hearing.

  A motion was made by Council Member Herrera Avila, seconded by Mayor
  Menchaca, to adopt Resolution No. 25-19 updating the Master Fee Schedule for
  Fiscal Year 2025-2026, as amended to include the same discounts for City
  commissioners as employees.

I  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HERRERA AVILA, WU, CHAN, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. COMPREHENSIVE CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION STUDY REPORT

  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Macias made the presentation.

  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz clarified that this is a receive and file report
  and cautioned the City Council against stating positions on any of the findings as
  labor negotiations are currently in progress.

I  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included that a report recommendation to add two position
  classifications is not a recommendation to hire for those positions; benchmark use;
  position title and job description changes and additions; and next steps.

  MGT Lead Consultant Jessica Ancona commented positively on working with City
  staff.

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT - None.

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Chan reported on his attendance at an Asian American Heritage Month
  celebration at Los Angeles Police Department Headquarters, Pet Wellness Day at the
  Mission Playhouse parking lot, San Gabriel Fire Service Day, Chinese American Citizen's
  Alliance meeting, Taste of South Pasadena fundraiser for Rotary Club, an Asian
  American Heritage Month celebration hosted by Southern California Edison, the
  annual Play Day celebrating the 60th Anniversary of the La Laguna Playground at

I  Vincent Lugo Park, Monrovia Days, and a San Gabriel Historical Association dinner and
  tour at the Mission Playhouse.

  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at SO Plus AAPI Heritage and Menta l
  Wellness event, Assemblymember Mike Fang's Pet Wellness event, Fire Service Day,
  JCOA Parents' Day, District 4L2 Lions Club Mother's Day event, Mother's Day event
  and model competition at the Sheraton, and San Gabriel Play Day at La Laguna.

  Council Member Herrera Avila reported on his attendance at Assemblymember Mike
  Fang's Pet Wellness Day, San Gabriel Fire Service Day, Spectrum Noticia's National

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 4  May 20, 2025
   Launch reception for their 24/7 Spanish language national news network, Del Mar
  School tour with Superintendent Symonds, La Laguna Playground event honoring the
  Dominguez family, LA International Zen Business Wisdom seminar at the Sheraton,
  and West California Art Center graduation ceremony.

  Council Member Wu reported his blood donation at the Carpenters Training Center in
  Whittier, and reported on his attendance at Fire Service Day, the JCOA Parents' Day
  event, and the World Master Games hosted by Taipei City and New Taipei City.

I  Mayor Menchaca commented briefly on the trip to the World Master Games and
  commended Council Member Wu for being a leader in this area; reported her
  attendance at the Pet Wellness event and Fire Service Day, and announced San
  Gabriel's Memorial Day ceremony in partnership with the San Gabriel Veterans
  Memorial Coalition, to be held on May 24, 2025, from 10:00 - 11 :00 A.M. at Plaza Park.

  10. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:05 P.M. in memory of Juana Beatriz Gutierrez.

  Respectfully submitted:

I

I

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 4  May 20, 2025
